newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma says Suu Kyi manipulated by CIA.
newsitem.headline: Burma says Suu Kyi manipulated by CIA.

text.p: Burma's state-run media continued its attacks on democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi on Saturday, saying she was being manipulated by the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) to try and bring down the government.
"It is not that the CIA is having her play a ploy to be able to get political power as a democracy leader," a commentary in the official New Light of Myanmar said.

"The aim of putting her onto the political stage is just to have her plotting to bring down the ...government that is striving day and night and making progress all round while maintaining stability, peace and tranquillity in the country."
Burma's media is tightly controlled by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) and considered to be the mouthpiece of the government.

Calling Suu Kyi "Mrs Michael Aris" in reference to her marriage to the British academic, the commentary said Aris -- who lives in England and is rarely allowed to visit Suu Kyi -- and the CIA were pulling the strings and Suu Kyi was acting as their puppet to help cause unrest in the nation.

"(The CIA) are pulling strings from behind, just to have her disparaging, vilifying and obstructing everything being done by (the) government and instigating the unwitting youths in devious ways to create disturbances," the commentary said.

The SLORC has accused Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party of colluding with students involved in rare sit-in protests in Rangoon last week. It has also accused her of conspiring with Western governments, especially the United States, to try and upset the nation's peace.
The government detained Suu Kyi's close aide Kyi Maung for questioning about his role in the protests.
Up to 1,000 university students staged a sit-in protest early on Wednesday at an intersection about two km (1.2 miles) from Suu Kyi's residence.
Suu Kyi, who lived under house arrest for six years and was released in July 1995, was urged by security officials from the government and the NLD not to leave her house during the protests.
Diplomats quoted an NLD official as saying Suu Kyi had been put under virtual house arrest but a government official told Reuters on Friday Suu Kyi was under no restrictions.

But there was still no word from her on Saturday, as the roads leading to her house remained blocked. Her telephone has not worked since late September, when the line was apparently cut as the SLORC took various steps to prevent the NLD from holding a party meeting.
